run.change_description:
9f99628001cdc79c2d49775cfc3b3ab35b77fb85
fix(redis2): remove orphaned directory index members on listing

ListDirectoryEntries skipped index members whose value key was gone and
left them in the ZSET, so the per-directory child index grew without
bound under any TTL workload. Mirror the ZRem the logical-expiry branch
already performs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

6c8fde6642cd428e884cc9c9d88c9aaa189c4bf1
fix(redis2): keep the index member when a concurrent insert recreates the value

The orphan cleanup removed the member unconditionally, so an InsertEntry
landing between FindEntry and the ZRem left a live value with no index
member, invisible to listings until another InsertEntry on that path.
UpdateEntry does not re-add it, so the loss persisted.

Restore the member when the value is present again after the removal.
The value key and the directory index key hash to different slots, so a
Lua script or MULTI over both is not available to the cluster store.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

summary.intent: Stop the redis2 per-directory ZSET index from accumulating members whose value key is gone by removing them during `ListDirectoryEntries`, without ever dropping the member of an entry that a concurrent `InsertEntry` recreates.
summary.issue_fit: Issue alignment unavailable: no originating issue; intent comes from the user-supplied pull-request packet for seaweedfs/seaweedfs#10735 and the two commit messages. The cleanup and the concurrent-recreate guard work when every read hits the primary, but on `redis_cluster2` with replica reads the guard is bypassed and live entries can lose their index member.
summary.coverage: Full `main...review-head` diff (2 files) reviewed at `6c8fde6`, together with InsertEntry/UpdateEntry/DeleteEntry/FindEntry, the three redis2 client constructors, `FilerStoreWrapper.ListDirectoryEntries`, and go-redis v9.21.0 cluster read routing. Untracked `.mcp.json` in the clone is outside the committed range and was not reviewed. Two verifier batches ran: the replica-read finding is confirmed, a listing-cancellation candidate was refuted (the wrapper already detaches the context), and the claim that only `redis.Nil` reaches the cleanup holds.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -count=1 -v ./weed/filer/redis2` offline at `6c8fde6`: exit 0, package compiles, all four new tests SKIP because no Redis server is available (`RUN_REDIS_TESTS` unset), so their assertions were settled by code trace only.
Reviewer ran `go vet ./weed/filer/redis2` and `gofmt -l weed/filer/redis2` at `6c8fde6`: both clean.
The PR packet's reported redis-server 8.x runs (fail on master, pass with the change) are author-supplied output without a reviewable log at this head; recorded as unavailable.

findings.title: Confirm the value is gone on the primary before dropping its index member
findings.trigger: On `redis_cluster2` with `routeByLatency = true` or `useReadOnly = true`, go-redis sends the read-only `GET` in `FindEntry` and the `EXISTS` in `removeOrphanedDirectoryListMember` to a replica or the closest node, while `ZREM` always goes to the primary, so a listing that runs while that replica lags behind a just-completed `InsertEntry` sees the member but gets `redis.Nil` for the value.
findings.impact: The cleanup removes the live entry's member on the primary, the confirming `EXISTS` asks the same lagging replica and returns 0, and the restoring `ZAddNX` is skipped, so the entry disappears from every later listing and from `DeleteFolderChildren` until another `InsertEntry` on that path, because `UpdateEntry` never re-adds it; at the merge-base the same stale read only hid the entry from that one listing.
findings.change: Confirm the value's absence on the primary that owns the value key's slot before keeping the removal, for example by issuing the `EXISTS` through `(*redis.ClusterClient).MasterForKey` when `store.Client` is a cluster client, or skip the orphan removal when the client may read from replicas.
findings.source: Commit 6c8fde6: “Restore the member when the value is present again after the removal.”

observations.fact: The scaffold names the `redis_cluster2` replica-read switch `readOnly`, but the store reads `useReadOnly`, so replica reads are reached only through `routeByLatency` (which go-redis turns into read-only routing) or the undocumented `useReadOnly` key.

Even with primary-only reads, a racing re-insert still loses its member when both the confirming `EXISTS` and the restoring `ZAddNX` fail with a non-context Redis error after the `ZREM`, because the helper discards those errors.

tasks.premise: With primary-only reads, an InsertEntry racing the orphan cleanup for the same path always leaves the member in the index once both finish.
The cleanup is reached only when GET returned redis.Nil; every other FindEntry failure leaves the index untouched and ends the listing with an error.
